Bangkok is truly the straw of the hour for the simple hat. It is a soft, pliable, closely woven fabric, light and airy in appearance, and—when genuine—fairly expensive. But by "fairly expensive," one means that its cost is fair when one considers its value to the mode. It has all the ethic, strength and wearability of the felt, which is recommendation enough to any fabric.
Ballibunt, too, is expensive, when compared with some of the more, familiar straws. But it is aristocratic in appearance as well as in quality, and its easy adaptability to the creasing and molding of the new spring shapes makes it a welcome addition to the fabric array. Both Bangkok and Ballibunt are accented with "reverberation, felt appliances or trim-savings and flowers.

text: Crowns are changing. We had the square crown—a few could wear it well, then we had an epidemic of heaked, doubted, crossed crowns—we aren't over it yet; but there is a newer dome-shaped crown that is attracting attention. It may be newer than the peak, but it is difficult to wear and no one can prophesy much for a style that is so handicapped at the start. It may be said, however, that the general tendency is toward crowns that conform more closely to the shape of the head. This is good.

label: text
text: Since the mode is, in general, a riot of colour, we have a perfect right to expect a generative use of it in millinery especially spring millinery. As the season advances there will be a deal of white—Paris predicts a white summer. But Paris is not infallible when it comes to what we wear over here and a safer prophecy will include the pastels, the jewel and rainbow shades—especially in felt—and black and navy.
